newsitem.title: UK: Guinness, Grand Metropolitan announce merger.
newsitem.headline: Guinness, Grand Metropolitan announce merger.

text.p: Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc Monday announced surprise plans for a merger worth more than 20 billion pounds ($32.5 billion), creating the world's seventh-largest food and drinks company.

The deal will also form a leading spirits and wine company, bringing together brands such as GrandMet's Smirnoff vodka, Bailey's and Cinzano with Guinness-owned Johnnie Walker and Bell's Scotch whisky and Gordon's gin.
It also unites GrandMet's strong U.S. food interests through Burger King and Pillsbury with Guinness' brewing operations, which include its famous stout ale.

Guinness shareholders will retain their shares in the new company, to be called GMG Brands, while GrandMet shareholders will receive one GMG share for every GrandMet share they hold. This would leave GrandMet shareholders with 52.7 percent of GMG.

Stocks in the two companies surged after the news as investors and analysts looked to cost savings from the deal as well as a planned one-time cash handout to shareholders of 60 pence per share, worth about 2.4 billion pounds ($3.9 billion).

At Friday's share prices, the combined value of the group was 20.61 billion pounds ($33.5 billion), making it the seventh-largest food and drinks company worldwide and Britain's eight-largest publicly held company.

The value of the deal was boosted to around 23 billion pounds ($37.4 billion) as GrandMet shares rose 66 pence to 581 after touching 585 and Guinness shares jumped 68 pence to 584-1/2 after also a high of 588.

The companies said Guinness non-executive director Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods and drinks group LVMH Moet Hennessy, which has a 14.2 percent stake in Guinness, voted against the deal. He suggested an alternative that would involve a combination of the three spirits and wines businesses of GrandMet, Guinness and Moet Hennessy as an independent listed group.
But GrandMet Chairman George Bull told reporters the companies had looked at all alternatives and were "absolutely convinced that the merger ... is in the interests of all our shareholders."

Bull also said he did not expect the merger to face regulatory problems as it would give the group less than 10 percent of accessible world spirits markets. "We are entirely confident that we will be able to obtain the agreement of the regulatory authorities both here in Europe and also in the United States and elsewhere," he said.

Bull will initially chair the new group jointly with Tony Greener of Guinness, but will retire as planned in July 1998, leaving Greener as sole chairman. GrandMet's John McGrath will be chief executive, with the rest of the board made up of a balance of directors from both firms.

Bull said the move would "create a combined spirits and wine company which will truly be a world leader so it will be able to grow faster at that stage than either would be able to do on its own. If you put the whole lot together then you achieve a much faster growth rate together than either could achieve on their own," he said.
GMG Brands' four divisions will be United Distillers and Vintners, the combined spirits and wines business, Pillsbury, Burger King and Guinness Brewing Worldwide.

The merger gives Guinness an increased interest in North America through GrandMet's Pillsbury and Burger King food divisions, while GrandMet shareholders will benefit from the Guinness spirits business in emerging markets.
Pilsbury brands include Green Giant vegetables and Haagen-Dazs icecream. Guinness stout is one of the world's most widely distributed beers, brewed in 50 countries and sold in about 150.

The companies said the merger would generate cost savings of about 175 million pounds ($285 million) a year in the third year of trading by integrating the sales force around the world, pruning back at head offices and savings in production.

The companies did not detail possible job losses, but Guinness Chairman Tony Greener told BBC radio it was possible there would be around 2,000 job losses out of a combined work force of 85,000. The losses wold be distributed around the world and take place gradually over three years, he said.
Total costs of achieving the savings are expected to be about 375 million pounds ($610 million), of which 300 million ($488 million) would be cash and the balance accounting writedowns.
GrandMet brought forward announcement of its first-half results to coincide with the merger news. Pre-tax profit rise 3.5 percent to 471 million pounds ($766 million) before charges.
